inputs.share_count_basis: 553,333,400 issued shares (share capital RMB553,333k at par RMB1, H1 FY2026 interim note 24). Held FLAT. The restricted share incentive scheme is funded with existing shares bought by a trustee, so it is non-dilutive; diluted weighted average 552.241m is lower only because trustee-held unvested shares are excluded. Issued count used as the conservative divisor.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents RMB10,131.5m + deposit certificates at amortised cost RMB2,296.5m (principal RMB2,205.9m, 1.55-2.6% fixed, 24-36 month tenor; H1 FY2026 note 18), both at 30 June 2026. No borrowings or bank loans (interim MD&A). Lease liabilities RMB89.4m are excluded because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). The FY2025 final dividend of RMB775.2m was still payable at 30 June 2026 and is deducted in equity_bridge. Around RMB2.1bn of this cash is matched by contract liabilities (prepaid management fees) - operating float, not surplus in a liquidation sense - and all of it is onshore RMB; see valuation_philosophy for the haircut a reader may wish to apply.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: equity-settled share-based payments were a CREDIT of RMB17.3m (forfeiture reversal of the 2022 restricted share scheme); FY2024 RMB26.3m, FY2023 RMB39.0m. Treated as 0 for FY0 (the reversal is not a recurring benefit) and projected at 0% - only 11k dilutive scheme shares remained at H1 FY2026. Equity-award taxes 0 in every year. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2024, FY2025 or H1 FY2026 (financing cash flows). FY2022-23 outflows of RMB46m/RMB120m were trustee purchases for the restricted share scheme. The flat count is a modelling convention the company is not funding, but with no SBC charge there is nothing to fund.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1748 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X on 2026-10-23 (inverse HKD->CNY 0.8512). Per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1748 for the HKD canonical figures. No dual listing exists for a parity check (Poly Property has no A-share line); the rate is consistent with the USD/CNY ~7.1 and USD/HKD ~7.8 crosses.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China government bond ~1.8% + beta 1.0 x China H-share equity risk premium ~6.5% + 1.7% for SOE-subsidiary governance (related-party cash transfers to the parent are observed, not hypothetical), onshore-trapped RMB cash and a thin H-share float = 10.0% cost of equity, which is the WACC because the company carries no debt. The same 10% is used in all three scenarios; scenario-specific risk lives in the flows and the weights, not in per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Lease principal (RMB29.4m FY2025, financing) plus lease interest (RMB3.9m, operating) = RMB33.3m, 0.19% of revenue, charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path 0.2%. Lease liabilities (RMB42.5m current + RMB46.9m non-current at 30 June 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (~RMB350m of the RMB379m reported).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is small (RMB192m stock; RMB18.4m of FY2025 profit, 1.2%). Folded into the cash-tax driver: 24.1% cash tax on EBIT ex interest income + ~1pp NCI leakage = 25%. No NCI deduction in the bridge, so it is charged once. Check: FY0 EBIT ex interest 1,996 x 0.75 = RMB1,497m vs attributable net income ex after-tax interest income RMB1,494m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 2: non-US operating company, with the adaptations file applied for currency, leases, NCI and SBC-zero). Poly Property is an asset-light fee-for-service operator - 80% of revenue is recurring property management fees on 894m sq.m. under management - so its value is a stream of owner FCF plus a very large net-cash pile. A holdco/NAV model was considered because net cash is ~94% of the market capitalisation, but rejected: the cash is retained operating profit, not an investment portfolio, and the engine already adds it to EV; the matching-asset rule is satisfied by stripping the RMB73.6m of interest income from the flows. EBITDA margin is defined EX interest income (FY2025: 13.87%, i.e. reported EBITDA 2,449 less 74). FY0 owner FCF of RMB1,705m is flattered relative to a normal year: FY2025 capex was only RMB49m because the three-year prepaid carpark/clubhouse lease cycle (RMB855m FY2021, RMB840m FY2024, the next batch due ~FY2027) fell in other years, and lease principal sits in financing. The component build charges capex at a normalized 2.0% of revenue (~RMB280m/yr leased-asset renewals + ~RMB55m PPE), which is why year-1 owner FCF (~RMB1.57bn) is below FY0. Working capital: FY2023-25 net inflow averaged +23% of revenue change (contract liabilities and payables grew with scale) but trade receivables rose 29% in H1 FY2026 against +5% revenue and the impairment charge doubled, so base capture is set to 0%. Horizon 10 years; margins are mature so the test is satisfied, but the 10-year path lets the growth deceleration play out before capitalisation. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (structurally slower, low-multiple sector). Analysis.json was not yet available at build time; qualitative context is drawn directly from the H1 FY2026 interim and FY2025 annual report.

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend payable (RMB1.401/share) outstanding at 30 June 2026, paid after period end; price is ex-dividend
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim MD&A, accruals and other payables

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Revenue run-rate: FY2025 +4.8%, H1 FY2026 +5.2% (property management +11.9%, developer-linked and community VAS -17%/-14%). Equity CAGR (11%) rejected as the anchor: it is inflated by retaining half of earnings as idle cash under a ~50% payout, not by reinvestment at a return.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 11.1% exceeds revenue 3yr CAGR 7.8% by 43% - the gap is cash accumulation, not operating leverage. Revenue growth has decelerated every year since FY2021 (34% -> 27% -> 10% -> 8.5% -> 4.8%).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 376, FY2021 426, FY2022 1,204, FY2023 2,234, FY2024 1,297, FY2025 1,705 (RMB m). The 5-year figures are distorted by the leased-asset purchase cycle (FY2021 RMB855m, FY2024 RMB840m) and by the large working-capital inflow of FY2023; neither CAGR is a usable forward anchor. Owner-FCF CAGR is above reported-FCF CAGR only because interest income has fallen as deposit rates dropped, not because SBC is shrinking faster than cash flow.

base.growth_rationale: Managed GFA grows ~4-5%/yr (855m sq.m. FY2025 -> 894m at June 2026) with residential fee/sq.m. edging up (2.47 -> 2.52); base property management revenue grows high-single-digit while developer-linked VAS and community VAS keep shrinking, netting to ~5% group growth, fading to 2.5% as the parent's delivery pipeline thins.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA ex interest income 13.9% FY2025; H1 FY2026 gross margin -0.2pp with admin -0.4pp of revenue. Mix shift to lower-margin third-party and public projects offsets admin leverage and robotics/AI cost-out; drifts to 13.5%.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 2.0% = ~RMB280m/yr normalized leased-asset renewal (three-year prepaid carpark/clubhouse leases) + ~RMB55m PPE. D&A ex-ROU 2.0%; add-back and capex net to zero.

bear.capex_rationale: 3.0% of revenue models the parent extracting cash through larger related-party asset purchases (the FY2021 and FY2024 carpark/clubhouse batches were each ~5% of that year's revenue); D&A ramps to match as the prepaid-lease book grows.

scenario_narratives.base: Poly Property keeps compounding managed GFA at 4-5% a year on the back of Poly Developments' core-city pipeline (36% of contracted GFA, 54% of management revenue) and a third-party expansion engine winning ~RMB1.4bn of annualised contract value per half, while the two developer- and consumer-linked VAS lines keep shrinking at double digits until they are too small to matter (~20% of revenue today, down from 30%). Group revenue grows ~5% fading to 2.5%; the EBITDA margin ex interest income drifts from 13.9% to 13.5% as third-party and public-property mix dilutes it and robotics/AI cost-out only partly offsets wage inflation. Working capital is neutral: contract-liability and payable growth offsets the receivables build. Capex is charged at a normalized 2% of revenue so the three-year carpark/clubhouse lease renewals are not forgotten in the years they do not fall. Net cash of RMB12.4bn less the RMB775m dividend already declared is added in full.
scenario_narratives.bull: China's housing market stabilises in 2027, Poly Developments' deliveries recover and pre-delivery VAS stops shrinking; third-party wins in commercial/IFM and public scenic-area contracts (21.8% growth in commercial/office fees in H1 FY2026) lift group growth to 7% for three years. Fee collection rates improve under the state's property-service-quality programme, so working capital turns modestly positive again (+10% of revenue change), and the company's robotics pilots (cleaning robots in 100+ projects, AI work-order dispatch) lift the EBITDA margin to ~14.8%. Payout rises further toward the sector's 60-70%, which is what would make the market pay for the cash.
scenario_narratives.bear: The property downturn runs longer: Poly Developments' deliveries fall, developer VAS and office leasing keep contracting, and the public/third-party portfolio proves lower-fee and slower-paying, so revenue stalls at zero growth for FY2028-29 before resuming ~2%. Fee-cut pressure from owners' committees and wage inflation compress the EBITDA margin to 11%. Trade receivables (already +29% in H1 FY2026 on +5% revenue, impairment charge doubled) keep absorbing cash at 15% of revenue change. Poly Developments itself is weakening fast (FY2025 net profit down ~84.5%, February 2026 contracted sales down ~37% year on year), and two general-manager changes in about seven months leave execution in new hands. The parent, under its own cash strain, extracts cash from the subsidiary through larger related-party prepaid-lease and asset purchases, modelled as capex at 3% of revenue indefinitely. The cash pile is never distributed beyond a ~50% payout. Terminal growth 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because of a single-counterparty dependency - the controlling shareholder is both the source of half the fee base and, through related-party asset purchases, the most plausible route by which the net cash fails to reach minority holders - and because the receivables trend in H1 FY2026 is the sector's leading indicator of distress. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right at once: a China housing stabilisation and a payout step-up. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: On an owner-FCF basis Poly Property is a ~RMB1.6bn/yr cash generator with no debt and a net-cash pile roughly equal to its entire market capitalisation; the enterprise value the market assigns to the operating business is close to zero. The house DCF therefore lands far above the price in every scenario, and the gap is not a modelling artefact - it is the market's discount for cash that is onshore, controlled by a state-owned parent, and returned only at a ~50% payout (6% yield). Readers who do not trust the cash should haircut it explicitly: every 10% haircut on the RMB11.65bn of post-dividend net cash is RMB2.1/share (HK$2.5). A 50% haircut still leaves the weighted value above the price. The valuation is roughly one-third cash and two-thirds operating business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Related-party cash extraction: the parent has twice (FY2021, FY2024) sold ~RMB850m of three-year prepaid carpark/clubhouse leases to the company; larger or more frequent transfers convert net cash into depreciating assets.

Receivables and collection: trade receivables rose 29% in H1 FY2026 against 5% revenue growth and the impairment charge doubled; a sustained working-capital drag would cut owner FCF below the modelled level.

Parent financial stress and management turnover: Poly Developments FY2025 net profit fell ~84.5% and its early-2026 sales ~37%; the subsidiary changed general manager twice in ~7 months (Analysis.json recent developments).
Parent delivery pipeline: 36% of contracted GFA and 54% of property management revenue come from Poly Developments projects; developer-linked VAS has already fallen 17% year on year.
Fee and margin pressure: owners' committees renegotiating fees, wage inflation, and mix shift toward lower-margin public and third-party projects.
Cash never reaching minorities: with no buybacks and a ~50% payout, the DCF credits cash the market may never see; the HKD value also carries CNY/HKD exposure.
Terminal-value sensitivity: ~50% of enterprise value sits in the terminal year at a 10% WACC; the sensitivity grid shows the swing.
